card.summary: RF Module, ESP32-S3 SoC, Wi-Fi 802.11b/g/n, Bluetooth, BLE, 32-bit, 3.3V, onboard antenna, SMD
Multiprotocol BLE/ANT/2.4 GHz/802.15.4 Cortex-M4F SoC, nRF52840 module

decision.reason: The slot calls for an MCU for a battery-powered Bluetooth handheld controller. The Raytac MDBT50Q (nRF52840) is a low-power BLE module with native USB and a Cortex-M4F core, which suits a wireless gamepad and long battery life. The ESP32-S3

card.summary: Multiprotocol BLE/ANT/2.4 GHz/802.15.4 Cortex-M4F SoC, nRF52840 module
Generic connector, single row, 01x02, script generated (kicad-library-utils/schlib/autogen/connector/)
JST ACH series connector, BM02B-ACHSS-GAN-ETF (http://www.jst-mfg.com/product/pdf/eng/eACH.pdf), generated with kicad-footprint-generator
Single cell Li-Ion/Po battery protection IC

decision.reason: A wireless handheld controller is best powered by a single rechargeable Li-ion cell. The 18650 holder is a real battery part for that. The 2xAA, 1xAA and 9 V holders are bulkier or give the wrong voltage. The JST connectors are not batterie

card.summary: USB-Friendly Li-Ion Battery Charger and Power-Path Management, VQFN-16
Single cell, Li-Ion/Li-Po charge management controller, 4.20V, Tri-State Status Output, in SOT23-5 package
1A Standalone Linear Li-ion/LiPo single-cell battery charger, 4.2V ±1% charge voltage, VCC = 4.0..8.0V, SOIC-8 (SOP-8)

decision.reason: The BQ24075 is a Li-Ion charger with power-path management, so the controller can run from USB while the battery charges and keeps working when the battery is depleted or absent. That suits a handheld, battery-powered wireless controller. C
